name: Cyhyreath

attributes.attribute: sends the reader to the Caointeach entry
An unseen bodiless voice that groans before death, loudest when disaster or epidemic brings many deaths
Bound to south Wales, east Dyfed, the three Glamorganshires, and the Towy River
Weeps for natives who die far from home and may have begun as a goddess of streams

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cyhyreath names a Welsh spectral figure. MacKillop also records the spelling cyheuraeth. One encyclopedia gives it no separate account and sends the reader to Caointeach. MacKillop gives the figure its own article. The Cyhyreath resembles the Caointeach heard in Gaelic Scotland and the Weeper mourned in English tradition. People usually meet it as an unseen voice without a body. Listeners hear it groan before death arrives. It cries out most when a disaster or an epidemic brings many deaths at once. Its haunts lie in south Wales, in east Dyfed, and in the three Glamorganshires. Dyfed covered Carmarthenshire until 1974. It is heard most near the Towy River. As with the Irish Banshee, the Cyhyreath weeps for natives who die far from home. MacKillop suggests the figure began as a goddess of streams.

okr.objective: Cyhyreath is the Welsh death voice of south Wales, an unseen cry that warns of coming deaths.
key_results: The Cyhyreath parallels the Caointeach in Gaelic Scotland and the Weeper in English tradition.
It groans before death, above all when disaster or epidemic brings many deaths.
Its range covers south Wales, east Dyfed, the three Glamorganshires, and the Towy River.
As with the Banshee, it weeps for natives who die far from home.
Monaghan gives it no separate account and points to Caointeach.
